questions.stem: \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram where \(AC\) and \(BD\) are the diagonals. If \(\angle BAD = 60^\circ\), \(\angle ADB = 90^\circ\), then what is \(BD^2\) equal to ?

A line through the vertex \(A\) of a parallelogram \(ABCD\) meets \(DC\) in \(P\) and \(BC\) produced in \(Q\). If \(P\) is the mid-point of \(DC\), then which of the following is/are correct ?
1. Area of \(\triangle PDA\) is equal to that of \(\triangle PCQ\)
2. Area of \(\triangle QAB\) is equal to twice that of \(\triangle PCQ\)
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
How many cubic metre of earth is to be dug out to dig a well of radius \(1\cdot 4\) m and depth 5 m ?
If the diagonals of a rhombus are \(x\) and \(y\), then what is its area ?

The lengths of sides of a triangle are \(3x, 4\sqrt{y}, 5\sqrt[3]{z}\), where \(3x < 4\sqrt{y} < 5\sqrt[3]{z}\). If one of the angles is \(90^\circ\), then what are the minimum integral values of \(x, y, z\) respectively ?
What is the maximum number of circum-circles that a triangle can have ?
If an arc of a circle of radius 6 cm subtends a central angle measuring \(30^\circ\), then which one of the following is an approximate length of the arc ?

A ladder 5 m long is placed in a room so as to reach a point \(4\cdot 8\) m high on a wall and on turning the ladder over to the opposite side of the wall without moving the base, it reaches a point \(1\cdot 4\) m high. What is the breadth of the room ?
What is the area of the largest square plate cut from a circular disk of radius one unit ?
flags: Invented subtopic: the catalog's Mensuration 2D has no entry for an inscribed/circumscribed figure. 'Combined and Shaded Regions' is the nearest listed subtopic but this question asks for the area of the inscribed square itself, not of a region between two figures.

questions.stem: Out of 4 identical balls of radius \(r\), 3 balls are placed on a plane such that each ball touches the other two balls. The \(4^{\text{th}}\) ball is placed on them such that this ball touches all the three balls. What is the distance of centre of \(4^{\text{th}}\) ball from the plane ?
flags: Invented subtopic: the catalog's Mensuration 3D subtopics are all about surface area and volume, and this question asks for a distance in a three-dimensional packing configuration (no area or volume is computed). 'Cylinder, Cone and Sphere' would be a misleading fit.

questions.stem: A right circular cylinder just encloses a sphere. If \(p\) is the surface area of the sphere and \(q\) is the curved surface area of the cylinder, then which one of the following is correct ?
\(ABCD\) is a quadrilateral such that \(AD = DC = CA = 20\) units, \(BC = 12\) units and \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\). What is the approximate area of the quadrilateral \(ABCD\) ?

Let \(PQRS\) be the diameter of a circle of radius 9 cm. The length \(PQ\), \(QR\) and \(RS\) are equal. Semi-circle is drawn with \(QS\) as diameter (as shown in the given figure). What is the ratio of the shaded region to that of the unshaded region ?
questions.figureNote: p13, right column, printed directly under the bare number '90.' and above the question text. Crop the whole circle with its horizontal diameter and the four point labels P, Q, R, S (P at the left end on the circle, Q and R the interior points, S at the right end on the circle) — the labels are essential. A second, smaller arc springs from Q and lands at S above the diameter; the hatched region is the part of the upper half bounded by the big circle and that inner arc. Include the hatching and both arcs; nothing below the circle is needed.
flags: Printed wording: the stem says 'Let PQRS be the diameter of a circle' where PQRS is four collinear points ON a diameter, not a segment. Transcribed exactly as printed; not repaired.

questions.stem: What is the area of the shaded region in the given figure, if the radius of each of the circles is 2 cm ?
questions.figureNote: p14, left column, printed directly under the bare number '91.' and above the question text. Three equal circles arranged in a cluster, each touching the other two; their centres are labelled A (upper left), B (upper right) and C (lower centre), and the triangle joining A, B, C is drawn. The small three-cornered region enclosed by the three arcs at the centre of the cluster is hatched. Crop all three circles in full plus the labels A, B and C and the drawn triangle; the hatched centre must be legible.

questions.stem: In the given figure, what is the area of the shaded region ?
questions.figureNote: p14, left column, printed directly under the bare number '92.' and above the question text. A circle with a rectangle inscribed in it, all four rectangle vertices on the circle. Four measurement labels must all be inside the crop: '6\(\sqrt{3}\) units' printed just BELOW the rectangle's top side (inside the rectangle), '6 units' printed inside near the left side, '6 units' printed inside near the right side, and '6\(\sqrt{3}\) units' printed just BELOW the rectangle's bottom side. The circular segment above the rectangle's top side is hatched. Crop the whole circle including the lower arc and every one of the four labels.

questions.stem: In the given figure, if \(\frac{y}{x} = 6\) and \(\frac{z}{x} = 5\), then what is the value of \(x\) ?
questions.figureNote: p14, right column, printed directly under the bare number '93.' and above the question text. A horizontal double-headed straight line with a point on it, from which two rays are drawn upward (one leaning left, one leaning right, both arrow-headed). Three angle labels at that point, all of which must be in the crop: 'x' lowest-left, just above the line; 'y' above it between the two rays; 'z' to the right of the steeper ray, between it and the rightward part of the line. Crop the full width of the horizontal line plus both ray arrowheads.

questions.stem: \(ABCD\) is a trapezium, where \(AB\) is parallel to \(DC\). If \(AB = 4\) cm, \(BC = 3\) cm, \(CD = 7\) cm and \(DA = 2\) cm, then what is the area of the trapezium ?
